patch.value: A settings read of a missing settings.json carries no snapshot, so a later write replaces a file another process created meanwhile (a first-run telemetry opt-out can be lost)

readSettings on a missing settings.json returns cloned defaults with no persist-source snapshot, and writeSettings treats such settings as caller-constructed: it replaces the whole document without reconciling against what is on disk. Every other read carries a snapshot, and its write reconciles leaf by leaf under the settings lock, so a concurrent edit to an untouched leaf survives and a conflicting one refuses. Reproduced on 2026.11.4 dist with a sandbox root: read A of the missing file, writer B records telemetry.enabled=false with first_run_prompt_completed=true, then A writes enabled=true and the stored file says enabled=true; the opt-out is lost. The same sequence over an existing file keeps enabled=false. Both consent writers that prompt and then write are affected on a fresh install: the runtime first-use prompt in core/telemetry/consent.ts and the pm init wizard in sdk/init.ts. The init wizard narrows the window by re-reading consent after its prompt (PR 1661 review), but the read-to-lock gap still clobbers when the file did not exist at that read. Found while answering a CodeRabbit finding on PR 1661 for the closed pm-gh1660; it is the missing-file residual of the closed lock-free settings family pm-bgcu.

A missing-file settings read carries a snapshot (or equivalent marker) so writeSettings reconciles against the document present under the lock; a spec reproduces the read-missing, concurrent-create, stale-write sequence and shows the concurrent telemetry opt-out survives; a first write to a still-missing file behaves exactly as today; caller-constructed settings without a read keep their documented whole-document replacement

A write from settings read while settings.json was missing reconciles against an empty stored document when the file has appeared, so a concurrent writer's leaves survive or the write refuses as stale_settings_snapshot
The write replaces the concurrently created settings.json wholesale; a recorded telemetry opt-out flips back to enabled

value.text: Scope update from the same PR 1661 review round. The pm init wizard no longer depends on this item for consent: its write passes the new WriteSettingsOptions.skipIfStored compare-and-set, consulted under the settings lock, so a consent choice stored by another process, even in a file that did not exist at the re-read, is kept. Still open here: the runtime first-use prompt in core/telemetry/consent.ts still writes without that check, so it can replace a concurrently created profile; when pm init targets the global profile itself, its create write replaces a concurrently created file; and any missing-file read loses a concurrent writer's non-consent fields. The first is a one-line skipIfStored adoption plus a kept message; the general fix is the missing-file snapshot this item describes.

patch.value: readSettings on a missing settings.json returns cloned defaults with no persist-source snapshot, and writeSettings treats such settings as caller-constructed: it replaces the whole document without reconciling against what is on disk. A successful read of an existing, valid settings.json carries a snapshot, and its write reconciles leaf by leaf under the settings lock, so a concurrent edit to an untouched leaf survives and a conflicting one refuses. Fallback reads (unreadable, malformed or schema-invalid files) carry none either; they take the separate fallback write path. The init wizard narrows the window by re-reading consent after its prompt (PR 1661 review), but the read-to-lock gap still clobbers when the file did not exist at that read.
